user.title: StormGuard
user.description:
StormGuard publishes weather risk events ("risk started" / "risk ended") to Home Assistant. Your automations decide what your devices do — the app never sends commands.

A secret webhook ID will be generated for the app.

data.allow_remote: Accept events from outside the home network

data_description.allow_remote: Turn on if your phone should also publish when it is away from home (Nabu Casa or an https external URL). Off: only requests from your local network are accepted; remote requests are silently dropped.

pair.title: Pair the StormGuard app
pair.description:
Open this link on the phone that runs StormGuard: {link}

```
{raw_link}
```

**Or enter manually** in StormGuard → Alerts → Smart home:

- Server address: `{base_url}`
- Remote address (https): `{remote_url}`
- Webhook ID: `{webhook_id}`

The webhook ID is a secret: anyone who knows it can send events to your Home Assistant. Then press **Send test event** in the app — the *Last event* sensor updates and no device changes. Submit to finish.

error.no_local_url: Home Assistant has no local network URL. Set one under Settings → System → Network, then open this integration's options to get the link.
error.insecure_local_url: The local URL uses plain http on an address the app does not treat as a home network, so the app will refuse it. Use a local IP/hostname (e.g. http://192.168.1.50:8123) or https under Settings → System → Network.
error.no_remote_url: No https external URL (or Nabu Casa) was found, so the link only works on your home network. Set an external URL under Settings → System → Network.

abort.already_configured: StormGuard is already set up. Open its options to see the pairing link again.
